runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Recent form reads 04-772 and the single placing in similar going flags limited upside; naturally a deep closer but squeezed into midfield here by the number of hold-up types, so it will race in an unfamiliar tactical position that the STYLE_FIT tag rightly flags as a concern.|

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — lone front-runner who wins the maps positional battle by default, and six placings in recent form including two seconds suggest it knows how to compete; going OK and the controlled solo lead on soft ground represents its best opportunity to last home.|

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: A finisher with a worrying tendency to fade at the finish flagged in the data, and a form string of 489-09 in similar going (0W0P from 7) offers little encouragement; pushed into midfield by the redistribution logic, so it will race against its instincts from a position that compounds its lateness problem.|

runners_data.name: Far Ahead
runners_data.note: Showed a single recent second in similar going (2/8f/GOO) which provides the only meaningful form hook, but the horse is a genuine hold-up type having to track from midfield rather than the rear it prefers — a positional compromise that the STYLE_FIT discount reflects accurately.|

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field (3yo) with a second over 12f at Southwell on its CV and trainer Charlie Johnston firing at 6/52 over 14 days; races as a hold-up type and has the class ceiling of an OR-58 for a race where soft ground could expose any greenness, but a clear run from the outside might suit.|

races.paceDynamic: Book Of Life is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger to its lead in a field of only six, it will stride into an uncontested and wholly sustainable gallop from the outset on Good To Soft ground over 1m1f at Hamilton. The pace will be honest but controlled — Book Of Life dictating its own rhythm rather than being hustled — which means fractions are unlikely to stretch the field early, compressing the race into a stamina test through the final two furlongs. Falcon Nine, Storm On Jura, and Far Ahead are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map positions because the rear of this field is overcrowded with closers; none of them is genuinely comfortable tracking the pace, and that congestion behind Book Of Life will create a muddling mid-race dynamic. This race shape — a single unhurried leader setting a steady, energy-conserving tempo — strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late finish, but given the overcrowding at the back, the runner who can sit just off Book Of Life in the Prominent-to-Midfield zone without getting shuffled wide stands to benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Book Of Life (Cian Horgan, 3lb claimer) is the lone leader and if the apprentice misjudges the fractions even slightly on soft ground, it risks either going too fast too soon or dawdling and gifting the race to the closing pack — the rider's inexperience is the single biggest variable.

The three redistributed closers — Falcon Nine, Storm On Jura, and Far Ahead — will be bunched together racing out of their natural positions in midfield, creating a genuine traffic-jam risk on the run to the home turn at Hamilton; one of them getting shuffled wide or blocked could swing the result.
Storm On Jura's "fades in finish" flag is a serious concern on a soft surface over 1m1f — if it is prominent in the market, the going report alone should temper confidence sharply.

Royal Blaze has the most credible sim-going profile of the hold-up horses (3/15, one placing) and is ridden by Alex Jary for Ewan Whillans (0/13 in 14 days) — a trainer out of form, but the horse's course-style fit means it warrants tracking from the back.|

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen

runners_data.name: Classy Al

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan-ridden Goldie four-year-old with strong soft-ground form (1W3P from four relevant starts) who races prominently; a winner at 5f on soft and runner-up twice on soft recently, he is ideally positioned to sit on the pace and deliver a strong finish.|

runners_data.name: Top Juggler

runners_data.name: Call Margot

races.paceDynamic: Tiva is the confirmed front runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, should bowl along at a sustainable tempo on this 5f Hamilton track — soft ground will ensure the pace is honest without becoming a desperate gallop. Canaria Queen is the other prominent-going type and will press forward to sit just behind or alongside, giving Tiva something to think about but not enough to turn this into a true test of stamina. With the race run at a controlled, single-pace rhythm, horses who can travel close to the action and produce their effort from the two-furlong pole are best placed — prominent and mid-division horses with tactical speed suit this shape far better than genuine hold-up types needing a strong late surge. This field is notably hold-up heavy: Jordan Electrics, Solar Aclaim, Top Juggler, Jm Jhingree, and Classy Al all prefer to close late, but with only Tiva and Canaria Queen as natural pace setters, the closers will need a strong enough gallop to reel them in — Canaria Queen and Montezuma, travelling prominently, are most likely to secure the favourable positions near the pace.

watchPoints.text: Canaria Queen's draw and early stride are critical — if she jumps well and pushes to Tiva's shoulder, she could dictate terms herself and those caught flat-footed behind will struggle to close on soft ground.
Tiva's stamina under soft conditions is unproven at this trip (0W1P from two soft-ground runs) — watch for signs of stopping inside the final furlong if she has been asked to go hard early.

Jordan Electrics tops the weights at 143lbs and has a flagged tendency to fade in finishes; if the pace is modest, any early advantage she gains will evaporate late and she could block the run of horses behind.

Montezuma's trainer Jim Goldie runs three horses in this race (Jordan Electrics, Classy Al, Montezuma) — watch for any tactical riding that frees up the most fancied runner, likely Montezuma given his recent soft-ground placed form.

Top Juggler's redistribution from hold-up to midfield means Dale Swift may struggle to place him in a position that suits his natural style — if he drifts back to his true position, watch for a late challenge that may just fall short at 5f.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Last win came on soft over 6f just seven days ago and is the most lightly weighted runner in the field at OR 51; although a true hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map due to congestion, the amateur claim of Amie Waugh (3lb) could prove meaningful if the finish is tight

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Form figures include a recent fourth on soft over this trip and a win on good five furlongs; hold-up type stepping back up to 6f where soft ground may just stretch the stamina edge, and the horse's recent proximity in similar races keeps it competitive

runners_data.name: Emperor's Son

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: 29 days between runs is the longest layoff in the field and form figures show a cluster of fourth-place finishes without a win on record at this trip; soft-ground experience is limited to two runs for modest returns, and the redistribution away from natural position compounds the risks

races.paceDynamic: With all eight runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 6f Hamilton contest faces a genuine pace paradox — someone must lead, but no horse is bred to do it willingly. The early stages on soft ground are likely to be tardy and hesitant, with jockeys eyeing each other before the field reluctantly strings out into a tactical crawl that compresses into a sprint finish from the 2f pole. Stirrup Cup, Pop Star, and Iris Dancer have shown the best recent soft-ground form and possess the finishing speed to thrive when a race collapses into a late dash, whereas horses like Catalyse, Maldevious and Emperor's Son — all redistributed from their natural hold-up positions because the map cannot place every genuine closer at the rear — may find themselves shuffled wider or forward against their instincts. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than can realistically hunt late cover; Stirrup Cup, Iris Dancer, and Doon The Glen, each having won recently on soft, are best placed to exploit the final-furlong scramble, and this race shape squarely favours the horse with the sharpest late kick on softening turf over runners who need a genuine gallop to build into.

races.name: Hamilton Park Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Sound Janet
runners_data.note: Has placed form on soft going (2/11f/SOF, 2/12f/SOF) and handles the trip, but is a natural closer who will want to race deep — the map places her in midfield, though she is likely to be rearmost in reality; Oisin Orr is a strong jockey booking and Julie Camacho's 4/26 trainer strike rate over 14 days is modest.

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: Recent return nine days ago is a concern for fitness going into a mile-and-a-half soft test, and all five historical runs have come at shorter trips (7f-9f), making this a stiff stamina ask; a genuine hold-up type who could end up closer than ideal to the pace given the redistribution, with Jake Dickson claiming 7lb offering some compensation.

runners_data.name: Geo
runners_data.note: All career form has been recorded on Good ground with no soft-surface wins or places from two outings in similar conditions — the going may not suit, and having raced exclusively at 7f-8f, this is an unexplored trip; natural hold-up runner whose redistribution to midfield is a secondary concern relative to the going and distance queries.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form figures of 70080 make for grim reading, and tongue-tie is worn; likely to be asked to fill the front-running void left by Hot And Cold's absence, but whether Iain Jardine's seven-year-old has the quality to exploit a lead at these weights is very much in question.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on Good going and is course-unexposed as a three-year-old, which gives scope; Connor Beasley knows the Hamilton track well, and the step up to 12 furlongs is the main unknown — if the trip suits, her finishing form makes her a live contender in any scenario that doesn't demand a pure front-running display.

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good going earlier in her career and has placed at 9f, so the mile-and-a-half on soft is a double query — ground and trip — for Tim Easterby's three-year-old; David Allan is an experienced pilot who will position her sensibly, but the natural hold-up style means she needs the race to be run to suit.

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — the sole confirmed front-runner in this field is absent, which fundamentally reshapes the pace dynamic and removes the one horse likely to have led throughout; its vacancy creates a leadership vacuum that the remaining field is poorly equipped to fill.

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the sole confirmed front-runner here, but is a non-runner, which means this race is effectively devoid of a natural pace-setter — the burden of making the running will fall reluctantly on one of the prominent types such as Second Fiddle or Porth Eilian stepping forward from their more usual positions. With Good To Soft ground over a mile and a half at Hamilton, and no horse naturally keen to lead, the early gallop is likely to be steady, producing a race that develops late and rewards horses who travel smoothly before producing their finish. Sound Janet, Epidavros, and Geo are all genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because this field carries more closers than the rear of the field can accommodate — of the three, Sound Janet and Geo are most likely to actually find rear-of-field berths, while Epidavros may end up slightly closer than ideal. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven ability in soft ground who can produce a sustained late run, as the moderate early pace will leave a premium on finishing kick rather than front-running stamina.

watchPoints.text: Porth Eilian is the horse to watch most closely — as the most recent winner in the field and a three-year-old with unexploited course potential, Connor Beasley may send her forward to fill the Hot And Cold vacuum, and if she settles into an uncontested lead the combination of youth and finishing form makes her a serious winning threat.

Second Fiddle is likely to be pressured into making the running against her better instincts given the absence of Hot And Cold — monitor how Aiden Brookes positions her at the start, because if she is forced too wide or too forward she will be used up before the straight.

Sound Janet and Geo are both genuine hold-up horses who may find themselves trapped in a slowly-run affair with insufficient room to produce their late runs — watch for them being caught flat-footed if the field suddenly quickens from a modest gallop in the final two furlongs.

The Good To Soft going (officially reported for this race) is worth monitoring given how the card has been riding — if it deteriorates further toward Soft, that will increasingly suit horses with proven soft-ground form such as Sound Janet over those with exclusively Good-ground histories like Geo and Porth Eilian.

races.name: Scottish Racing Supporting #Racingwithpride Handicap

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up operator for Tim Easterby with genuine soft-going form (0W2P on similar), though stepping up to 1m½f for the first time is an unknown — David Allan rides and the horse has form figures of 1 and 2 in similar conditions, making it a live each-way option if the pace obliges.

runners_data.name: Whernside
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's lightly raced 3yo has placed consistently but lacks soft-ground experience in this record, having run primarily on Good to Standard; Connor Beasley takes the ride on a horse that holds up naturally and will need the pace to truly test the front-runner before getting involved.

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's confirmed pace-setter holds the tactical key to the whole race, and while their single win came at 7f on good ground, they carry a style-fit flag (0.90) for stepping into a longer-distance context — David Nolan will try to exploit the uncontested lead but stamina at 1m½f on soft ground is an open question.

runners_data.name: Tarmonbarry Kid
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's 3yo is the standout soft-ground performer in the field with a win on soft over 8f and a placed effort in similar conditions; Oisin Orr takes over and the horse's natural prominence means they sit in the ideal tactical position to track Spiritoftheblues and deliver a challenge without being exposed to the soft ground stamina test.

runners_data.name: Just A Gambler
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's gelding is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but, in this six-runner field, finds itself charted in midfield rather than its customary position at the rear — carrying a style-fit discount (0.92) and with just 0W1P on similar going in eight runs, the horse needs the race to develop in an unlikely way to make its presence felt.

runners_data.name: Attention Seeker
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner has run just eight days ago and returns quickly off a career-high in terms of frequency, with a form string of 770744 suggesting modest ability; a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping by field configuration, the horse carries a style-fit flag (0.90) and Shay Farmer's 5lb claim is unlikely to compensate for a lack of competitive form.

races.paceDynamic: Spiritoftheblues is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure from another natural leader — they will set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good To Soft ground over 1m½f at Hamilton. Behind them, Tarmonbarry Kid is the only other naturally prominent type likely to track closely, while Beyond The Bar, Whernside, Just A Gambler, and Attention Seeker are all hold-up operators who will be settled in behind the pace. The relatively sedate, uncontested tempo set by Spiritoftheblues plays directly into the hands of a horse sitting just off the leader and kicking from a prominent pitch, rather than those coming from deep who will need the pace to stretch the field. This race shape favours a prominent-to-midfield profile that can exploit the controlled gallop — true hold-up horses (Just A Gambler, Attention Seeker) are unlikely to get their natural position at the rear given the small field and soft ground compressing the pack, but their redistribution to midfield is artificial, not natural, so their finishing kick cannot be fully trusted.

watchPoints.text: Tarmonbarry Kid has the only proven soft-ground win in the field and Oisin Orr will look to track Spiritoftheblues from the outset — if they get a clean passage into the straight, their form profile makes them the most dangerous horse in the race.

Spiritoftheblues controls the tempo entirely on their own and any change in how David Nolan rides them — either quickening early or slowing to a crawl — could drastically alter the shape; watch the early fractions from this lone front-runner.

Beyond The Bar steps up significantly in trip to 1m½f for the first time; David Allan will need to judge the hold-up run perfectly, and if the pace is too slow, the horse may find itself with too much ground to make up on the turn.

Just A Gambler and Attention Seeker, both genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield by field size, may find soft ground over 1m½f actually helps them stay in closer contact than usual — worth monitoring whether they settle naturally or are forced wide chasing their position early.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a sim-going figure of 6/14 and a placed effort on soft last time; Andrew Mullen rides and Iain Jardine's yard is in fair nick at 3/21 over 14 days — the 13-day return is no concern, and this 1m3f trip extends his best distance but soft ground may offset that.

runners_data.name: Galahad Threepwood
runners_data.note: 552 days off the track (406 jumping) is a major query on comeback fitness; Ben Pauling's 14-day strike rate of 6/41 is modest, and while this horse's natural instinct is to be held up for a late run, the long absence means it cannot be trusted to reproduce anything near its best today.

runners_data.name: Roger Henry
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and returns just 15 days after his last run; Lizzie Quinlan's small yard has a 2/9 14-day record; his form is built around AW surfaces (STA) and his only soft-turf run produced 4th over 11f — the move to soft Hamilton turf is a genuine concern for a horse who prefers to wait and finish.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with one Hamilton placing from 15 attempts on similar going; Jim Goldie's yard fires at 7/30 over 14 days so trainer form is positive, but Annandale's natural style of sitting last and grinding — now pushed into a midfield slot — means he may not get the true strong pace needed to reel runners in.

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: A four-year-old whose best form comes on good ground (won 12f/GOO, placed twice on soft/AW), and the step up to 1m3f soft is a new test; Amie Waugh claims 3lb which helps the handicapper's assessment, and at OR 53 the weight is lenient enough, but he races against type when pushed forward and his four-place record on soft merits respect rather than blind faith.

runners_data.name: Stepanov
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride for Edward Bethell, whose 3/31 14-day record is quiet; the three-year-old has placed five times from his last six starts including a second on soft, and stepping up to 1m3f represents a natural progression — the sole runner here with any realistic argument for securing a forward position without truly racing against type.

runners_data.name: Regulus Black
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's juvenile won over 10f on good at Hamilton last time out, which is highly relevant course form; Sam James continues the partnership and the step from 10f to 1m3f on soft is the key question — his style as the only front-runner gives him full control of tempo, and the STYLE_FIT flag notes he may be racing slightly out of his most comfortable role in this particular field configuration.

races.paceDynamic: Regulus Black is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m3f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, Sam James can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground without any pressure from behind. The remainder of the field — Tee Aitch Aye, Galahad Threepwood, Roger Henry, Annandale, Uncle Liam and Stepanov — are all hold-up or wait-and-see types who will be settled in behind, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. On soft ground over 1m3f at Hamilton with a lone leader setting a steady tempo, prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel smoothly and deliver a sustained finish will be favoured over pure late-closers who need a fast pace to burn off rivals in front. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; of those redistibuted to midfield, Stepanov and Uncle Liam are most likely to secure a realistic forward pitch given their profile and lighter weights, while Annandale and Galahad Threepwood — racing at longer odds and with bigger gaps since their last run — are less certain to find their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Regulus Black's ability to see out 1m3f on soft ground is the single most important factor in this race — if he fades inside the final two furlongs after leading throughout, the entire race shape collapses and the held-up horses inherit a very different contest.

Galahad Threepwood returns from 552 days off, including a jumping stint — watch for any early signs of ring-rustiness or reluctance that could compromise David Nolan's ability to place him effectively in a race with limited pace.

Stepanov and Uncle Liam are both natural hold-up types who may attempt to push forward; if both contest a prominent berth early, it could inject unexpected pace into the first half-mile and unsettle Regulus Black's intended solo lead.

The going is recorded as Good To Soft for the 5:52 but the race header flags Soft — monitor any late going update, as a softer surface would significantly extend stamina requirements and could bring Tee Aitch Aye's proven soft-ground record into sharper focus.

Annandale's sole placed run from 15 starts on similar going at Hamilton is a notable flag — Jim Goldie's yard is in form but the horse's course record suggests its chance may be more marginal than its stable companion Uncle Liam's.
